business-data-context

Bunkai data map

How data moves through Bunkai TMS. Built from the live staging schema (DBHub, 2026-11-13) and the target repo ../upex-bunkai-tms; paths in data-sources are relative to it, db: names live tables.

Overview

Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. Its data model enforces one structural rule: every ATC (Acceptance Test Case) is anchored to a User Story and to at least one of its Acceptance Criteria. Tests are ordered chains of reusable ATCs, so one ATC edit reaches every Test that chains it. Runs execute a Test against a project environment and freeze a snapshot of the chain, and Bugs are filed inside the test cycle (anchored to a Module, optionally to the Run step and ATC that found them).

Most business rules live in Postgres: about 130 bunkai_* RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER), Row Level Security per workspace role, and triggers. The app layer is thin, so the database is the best place to observe what really happened. Error codes are custom SQLSTATEs (45xxx) that the API maps to its error envelope.

Actors

ActorWhat they do with data
QA engineer (member)Authors stories, ACs, ATCs, Tests; runs manual executions; files Bugs
QA lead / adminConfigures projects, environments, members, Jira connection; closes Test Plans with a verdict
OwnerEverything an admin does plus billing, workspace deletion, export
ViewerRead only; cannot be a Bug assignee
Agent / CI (PAT)Same endpoints as the UI through a Personal Access Token: creates or submits runs, marks steps, files bugs
Systempg_cron sweeps, Vercel crons, Stripe webhook, notification triggers

Staging snapshot (2026-11-13): about 2,900 workspaces (2,974 community, 8 enterprise, 1 cloud), 20k ATCs, 5.6k Tests, 5.7k runs, 2.8k bugs. This volume is test residue from many QA runs: it says nothing about production usage.

Key relationships

  • Everything below a workspace cascades on delete (ON DELETE CASCADE), but the product never hard-deletes authoring data: modules, stories, ACs and ATCs are soft-deleted with archived_at.
  • atcs.user_story_id is RESTRICT: a story with ATCs cannot be physically removed. test_steps.atc_id is also RESTRICT: an ATC chained in a Test cannot be physically removed.
  • runs.test_id and runs.environment_id are RESTRICT: a Test or environment with runs cannot be deleted. run_atcs.atc_id and run_steps.atc_step_id are SET NULL: the snapshot outlives its source.
  • bugs.atc_id, run_id, run_step_id are SET NULL; bugs.module_id cascades. A bug always belongs to a module.
  • Users live in Supabase auth.users; most "created_by" style columns are SET NULL, while workspace owner, test creator and checkout or export requester are RESTRICT.

ATC: anchoring, archive and the dormant status column

  • An ATC must link at least one Acceptance Criterion of its own User Story. The "at least one" is enforced by the API validator (lib/atcs/validation.ts, zod min 1); the database only checks that each linked AC exists, is active and belongs to the story (45020). A direct DB insert could create an ATC with no AC.
  • Classification: layer UI, API or Unit; optional priority Critical, High, Medium, Low; optional technique Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise.
  • Search: trigger atcs_refresh_tsv rebuilds an English full-text vector from title and tags on every insert or update.
  • Archive and restore (bunkai_archive_atc, bunkai_restore_atc) are idempotent. While archived, updates to the ATC are rejected (45025). Trigger atcs_guard_archive_columns blocks clients from writing archived_at, archived_by or archive_batch_id directly (42501): only the RPCs can.
  • atcs.status (pass, fail, blocked, skipped, running, unrun) is dormant: no migration writes it, finishing a run explicitly does not touch it, and all 21,585 staging ATCs are unrun. Results live on run_atcs. Do not assert on atcs.status as a "last result".

Flow: create a workspace and its first project

  1. A signed-in user creates a workspace through bunkai_bootstrap_workspace, which inserts the workspace and the creator's membership row.
  2. Trigger workspaces_create_general_chat_channel creates the single general chat channel.
  3. Creating a project fires bunkai_enforce_project_limit_trigger (BEFORE INSERT) against the workspace's effective plan: community 3 projects, cloud 50, enterprise unlimited. Over the limit: project_limit_reached (45700).
PlanSeats (shown)Projects (enforced)RetentionPrice
community5330 days$0
cloud255090 days$24 per seat per month
enterpriseunlimitedunlimitedunlimitedn/a

Only the project limit is enforced in the database. Seat counts are display data (purchased_seats); nothing blocks a 6th member on community.

Flow: invite, join, remove and leave

  1. An active admin or owner invites by email with role viewer, member or admin (never owner). The token is stored hashed; the invite expires after 7 days.
  2. Accepting (bunkai_accept_workspace_invite, service role) re-checks that the inviter is still an active admin or owner ranked at or above the invited role. Errors: revoked or already accepted (45224), expired (45224), user already a member with an equal or higher role (45223).
  3. Removing a member (bunkai_remove_workspace_member): you cannot remove yourself (45220), an owner (45221) or the sole owner (45213). Side effects: every Bug assigned to that person is unassigned (bug.unassigned), the row is deleted, member.removed is logged.
  4. Leaving: refused if it is your last membership (45212) or you are the sole owner (45213).

Since 0118 clients have no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on workspace_members: every membership write goes through these RPCs.

Flow: author from story to Test

  1. Project → Module tree (nested; a rename rebuilds the materialized path of the module and all descendants; a sibling slug collision fails with 23505).
  2. User Story created as draft; Acceptance Criteria are ordered.
  3. Moving a story to ready_to_test requires at least one active AC (ac_required_for_ready_to_test, 45010). Removing the last active AC sends the story back to draft automatically.
  4. ATCs are written against the story and linked to ACs (see entity-atc).
  5. A Test chains at least one ATC (45120) in ordered positions (unique per Test). Tags: up to 20, 50 characters each, no commas; smoke, sanity, regression are reserved and lowercased; bunkai_set_test_tags replaces the whole set and logs test.tags_changed.
  6. automation_status defaults to manual-only; other values candidate, automated. It is a label, not a gate.

Flow: archive and restore (soft delete)

  • Archiving a Module (bunkai_archive_module_subtree) archives the module, all descendant modules and their stories, ACs and ATCs in one transaction, with one timestamp and (since 0117) one archive_batch_id.
  • Archiving a User Story (bunkai_archive_user_story, 0111) archives its live ACs and ATCs with one timestamp. Before 0111 the story's ATCs stayed live: the invariant is "archived parent means archived children", and every ATC reader filters only atcs.archived_at.
  • Restoring a Module (0117) is the exact inverse of one archive: it restores the rows carrying that batch id, not everything archived at the same time. Rows archived before 0117 have no batch id.
  • An ATC restored under a still-archived parent is handed to the parent's cascade state (stays hidden).
  • Archived rows are never physically deleted; Tests and Bugs are not part of the cascade.

Flow: manual run execution

  1. bunkai_create_run takes a Test, an environment and an executor_mode (human, agent or ci; anything else 45200). It inserts the run as running and logs run.started. A repeated call with the same (test_id, start_token) within 24 hours returns the existing run.
  2. Snapshot: each chained ATC becomes a run_atcs row (title copied) and each ATC step a run_steps row (content, input data, expected copied). Trigger run_atcs_set_source_atc_id records the source ATC once, for provenance.
  3. The executor marks steps (bunkai_mark_run_step) as passed, failed or blocked (anything else 45213; closed run 45212). Each mark stamps executed_at (the idle clock) and logs run_step.marked.
  4. After each mark the ATC result is recomputed: any step pending → pending; else any failed → failed; else any blocked → blocked; else passed.
  5. From a failed step the executor can file a Bug (see flow-bug-lifecycle).
  6. Finish (bunkai_finish_run): the caller supplies the verdict passed or failed (missing 45207); only a running run can finish (45206). Pending steps and ATCs become skipped. Logs run.finished {verdict, skipped_steps, via}.
  7. Abort (bunkai_abort_run): reason of at least 3 characters (45205), running only (45204). Same skip logic, logs run.aborted.

Business rule worth testing: the verdict is chosen, not computed. A run can be finished as passed with failed steps (manual path only; the automated path refuses that, see next flow).

Flow: agent and CI runs

Two paths for non-human executors:

PathHow it worksRules
StreamedCreate a run (executor_mode agent or ci), then mark steps one by one through the API with a PAT, then finishA Bearer re-report of the same step with the same result is a no-op; a different result is 45239. Inactive for 60 min → auto-aborted (see automatic processes)
One-shot submissionbunkai_submit_automated_run inserts a run already closed with the given verdict and all step resultsexecutor_mode stored as agent; verdict passed or failed (45232); verdict must agree with steps: passed with any fail, or failed with no fail, is 45235. Idempotent through run_submission_keys

Flow: file, assign and move a Bug

  1. A Bug is filed with severity P1 to P4, status open, a module and optionally the run, run step and ATC that found it.
  2. Trigger bugs_check_consistency (insert and update) keeps the anchors coherent: project in workspace (45304), module in project (45300), run in project (45305), run step in run (45306), ATC in project (45307).
  3. Assignment (bunkai_assign_bug) logs bug.assigned, bug.reassigned or bug.unassigned. The assignee must be an active member (45312) and not a viewer (45313).
  4. Status moves through bunkai_transition_bug_status one step forward at a time and logs bug.status_changed.
  5. Defect heatmap and density reports aggregate bugs per module.

Flow: plan, close and track a release

  1. A Test Plan is created open; Tests are added (unique per plan) or removed.
  2. Closing (bunkai_close_test_plan) needs a human verdict passed or failed (missing 45604, invalid 45605) and an optional summary up to 4,000 characters. Only the creator with write access, or an admin or owner, can close (45606). Closing freezes a progress snapshot.
  3. Reopening clears verdict, summary and snapshot.
  4. A Milestone has a name (unique per project, case-insensitive) and a target date between today and five years ahead (45502, 45503); no status column.
  5. Plans attach to milestones (unique pair). Readiness is computed on read: closed plans out of attached plans.

Flow: Jira connection and import

  1. An admin saves the workspace's Jira site (https://<name>.atlassian.net, else 45420), email and API token. The token goes to Supabase Vault; the table keeps only the secret id and clients cannot read the table. Connect, change and disconnect log jira_connection.* with only the site host.
  2. An import job is queued (one active job per scope). The runner claims it (running), pages Jira 100 issues at a time, converts descriptions from ADF to Markdown (truncated over 50 KB), extracts acceptance criteria, routes each issue to a module by Jira component (else an Inbox module) and upserts stories and ACs by external_id.
  3. Per-issue errors are collected and the job completes; a Jira auth failure or any thrown error fails the whole job.
  4. Deleting the connection purges the Vault secret (trigger workspace_jira_connections_purge_secret).

Bug push to Jira is prepared but not running: saving project tracker settings queues eligible bugs (sync_state = pending), yet no worker that moves them to syncing, synced or failed was found, and every staging bug is not_applicable.

Flow: upgrade, payment failure and grace

  1. The owner starts a checkout. A billing_checkout_sessions row is inserted open (one open session per workspace) before calling Stripe, and its id travels as client_reference_id.
  2. The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, then bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event upgrades workspaces.plan only when payment_status = paid, marks the session completed and logs workspace.plan_upgraded. Async payment failure or session expiry marks the session expired.
  3. Dedupe: the event id is stored in stripe_webhook_events after the session is found; an unknown session answers 5xx so Stripe retries.
  4. A failed renewal invoice sets payment_state = payment_failed and opens a grace period of 14 days from the event (a second failure does not extend it). Paying that invoice sets recovered, removes the grace row and logs workspace.payment_recovered. Out-of-order or stale events are ignored.
  5. Past the grace end, bunkai_effective_plan returns community for a cloud workspace. workspaces.plan is never rewritten and existing projects stay; only new projects hit the community limit.

Flow: workspace export

  • An export is requested (queued → running → completed or failed); trigger workspace_exports_log_requested logs the request.
  • The archive is stored in the private bucket workspace-exports.
  • Download requires a completed, unexpired export (else export_expired, 45803) and logs export.downloaded.

Flow: delete and restore a workspace

  1. Only the owner can delete (45900; already deleted 45901). The workspace is soft-deleted (deleted_at), access stops immediately, a tombstone row is written to workspace_deletions (no FK, so it survives the purge) and an email with a restore link (/workspaces/{id}/restore) is sent through Resend.
  2. Restore (bunkai_restore_workspace_deletion) works during 30 days (not deleted: 45902).
  3. A daily pg_cron job at 03:00 hard-deletes workspaces deleted more than 30 days ago and stamps purged_at on the tombstone. Everything under the workspace cascades.

Flow: attach evidence to a run step

  1. An upload creates a pending attachment and the file goes to the private bucket run-evidence; commit turns it committed.
  2. Limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP (checked by magic bytes, not only extension); 10 MiB per file, 50 MiB and 10 files per step, 250 MiB per run.
  3. A pending upload expires after 3 hours (committing an expired one: 45218). Terminal runs are read-only. Only the uploader can remove (45219).
  4. Deleting an attachment row queues its object in storage_cleanup_queue (not before 2 h 05 min later); the daily storage-cleanup cron deletes the files and expires stale pending rows.

Flow: notifications, mentions and the daily digest

EventWho is notifiedRules
run.finished, run.abortedThe run's executor onlyNot when the executor did it themselves through the browser (via cookie); a PAT or sweep close still notifies. Null executor: nobody
bug.assigned, bug.reassignedThe new assigneeEven when assigning to yourself
bug.status_changedReporter and assignee, de-duplicatedExcluding the person who made the change
bug.unassignedNobody
Chat @mentionEach mentioned active member, once per messageAlways in-app (mentions preference is locked); self-mention notifies nobody; an edit notifies only newly added people; max 50 mentions

Triggers on activity_log insert create the notifications, de-duplicated per source event and recipient. Preferences map run.* to run_lifecycle and bug.* to bug_lifecycle on two channels: both off = no row; in-app off and email on = a row hidden from the inbox but eligible for email.

Daily digest: a Vercel cron at 08:00 calls /api/v1/admin/send-digest; it emails each user with email enabled their unread items, once per day (notification_digest_log unique per user and date).

Staging (2026-11-13): no run is running; 2,384 aborted, 1,058 failed, 2,349 passed. The abort count is high because test sessions leave runs open and the sweeps close them.

State machine: run ATC and run step results

Both use pending, passed, failed, blocked, skipped. Steps start pending; an executor sets passed, failed or blocked; closing the run turns leftovers into skipped (never set by a person). The ATC result is derived from its steps after each mark (pending > failed > blocked > passed). A skipped step is not part of that rollup, so an ATC whose only non-passed step was skipped reads as passed (inferred from the rollup order; verify with a run before asserting it).

Integration: Supabase

Postgres, Auth (auth.users), Storage (run-evidence, workspace-exports), Realtime (run_atcs, run_steps, notifications, chat_messages), Vault (Jira tokens) and pg_cron. Every flow depends on it; if it is down the product is down. The QA roles qa_inspector_ro / qa_inspector_rw are how this repo reads the database.

Integration: Stripe

Data in: checkout and invoice webhook events change workspaces.plan, billing_checkout_sessions, workspace_billing_state and workspace_grace_periods. Data out: checkout session creation, invoices, payment method. Failure: with no key the billing routes answer 503 payment_processor_unavailable; a lost webhook leaves the session open until Stripe retries.

Integration: Resend

Outbound only: daily digest and workspace deletion or restore emails. A failure is logged per user and does not roll back the business change (the workspace is still deleted). The default sandbox sender only delivers to verified recipients.

Integration: Jira Cloud

Data in: stories and acceptance criteria through import jobs. Data out: none in practice (bug push is queued but not processed). Failure: the client backs off on 429; an auth failure fails the import job; per-issue errors are kept on the job.

Discovery gaps

  • I could not find the worker that moves bugs from sync_state pending to syncing, synced or failed. Bug push to Jira looks unimplemented; all staging bugs are not_applicable.
  • I could not find any writer of payment_state = retry_pending, nor the writer of checkout session canceled.
  • I could not verify the export expiry duration or any export cleanup job.
  • I could not verify the role the creator gets in bunkai_bootstrap_workspace (inferred owner) or the default plan of a new workspace (inferred community from staging data).
  • I could not verify whether UI or lib/ code writes atcs.status; migrations do not, and staging data shows it is never written.
  • The ATC rollup treatment of skipped steps is inferred from the rollup order, not observed.
  • The full event list of the daily digest candidates (run events) was not confirmed.
  • The legacy .context/business/business-data-map.md in the product repo (2026-08-24, design-time) still names Cloudflare R2, Sentry and PostHog; none exists in code. It was used as input only.
  • pg_cron jobs were read from migrations: the QA role cannot read cron.job, so the live schedule was not confirmed.
